new_lemmas.statement: On E:y²=x³-Dx, f=1/x and z=-x/y give z²=f/(1-Df²). For w=Df², log_E(z)=zG(w), where a0=1,a1=-2/5,a_j=(4j-5)a_(j-1)/(4j+1).
new_lemmas.proof: The recurrence gives 4w(1-w)G'+(1+w)G=1-w. Differentiating the curve identity gives z dw/dz=4w(1-w)/(1+w). Thus d(zG)/dz=(1-w)/(1+w)=(1+4Dz⁴)^(-1/2), with the normalized constant term and zero value at zero.
new_lemmas.conventions: Formal series identity on the curve, not equality of old and new finite polynomials in independent variables. D=11-6sqrt(2), with norm49. Normalized invariant differential and z=-x/y are fixed.

new_lemmas.proof: Keep H_*,41 contacts,anchor24 and scalar48. For a=|s|>(20H_*)² and B=max(|n|,|s|,|t|,|z|), nonzero Lucas defect gives B²-6<14H_*B^(3/2), contradiction. Hence log B>a-3. If beta!=n, p16 divisibilities give B²<7H_*N^(3/2)+6 and N<=2exp(h(beta))B, so log B<2log(32H_*)+3h(beta)<a/4, contradiction.
